operations.summary: Each bookmark row holds a URL, a title, a note, the date it was added and an archived flag; tags live in their own table and are joined through bookmark_tags. A URL is unique within a collection, and a collection is only a name column on the bookmark, not a table of its own. Deleting a collection therefore means deleting or moving every bookmark in it. The interface calls collections folders, which is the same thing under another name.
operations.details: docs/STACK.md describes the tables. The verification notes list a test in which adding the same URL twice to one collection fails with a clear message. The archived flag hides a bookmark from the default list without deleting it.

operations.summary: The maintainers chose plain SQL on the standard sqlite3 module over an ORM because the schema has five tables and few queries, and they wanted every query in one file, src/bramble/db.py, where a reviewer can read it without learning a framework, paste it into the sqlite3 shell and look at its plan with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN. They will revisit this only if the project ever needs a second database engine, which nothing on the roadmap asks for.
operations.details: pyproject.toml lists no database dependency besides the standard library. The verification notes say every query in db.py has a test that runs it against a fresh database.

operations.summary: The list shows the newest bookmarks first unless the user picks another order, and the choice is remembered per collection. Sorting by title ignores a leading 'The' or 'A'.
operations.details: The README describes the sort menu. The configuration file holds the default order; that file was not part of this material.

operations.summary: Imports of a few thousand bookmarks take minutes on Windows but seconds on macOS and Linux. The cause is not known yet. One guess in the notes is an antivirus scanning the database file after every commit.
operations.details: The verification notes record timings from a single Windows laptop. A commit message mentions trying one transaction per import, reverted because a single bad row then undid the whole import.

operations.summary: Open bugs that the README lists: renaming a tag to the name of an existing tag creates two tags with one name instead of merging them; the search box treats a hyphen as a word separator, so a hyphenated word is never found; archived bookmarks still count toward the number shown next to a collection; a URL with a trailing slash and the same URL without it are kept as two bookmarks; and dates are shown in UTC rather than local time.
operations.details: Each bug has a test marked as an expected failure in the verification notes, so fixing one makes that test pass and draws attention to it.

operations.summary: A release bumps the version in pyproject.toml, runs the whole test suite, builds the wheel and the source archive with python -m build, and tags the commit vX.Y.Z. The tag is pushed only after the new wheel installs cleanly in an empty virtual environment.
operations.details: The test configuration gives each test its own data folder, so the suite can run on a machine that also holds a real collection. The README gives the commands; nobody checked here that the wheel installs cleanly.

operations.summary: Tags are lowercase, use hyphens instead of spaces and are singular nouns, so 'recipe' rather than 'Recipes'. The interface rewrites a typed tag into that form before saving it. Older tags that break the rule stay as they are until someone edits them.
operations.details: The baseline document states the rule, and a commit made the interface rewrite tags as they are typed. The tag guide and its tests are not part of this material.

operations.summary: Planned next: syncing two machines through a shared folder (the sync design), faster search with an index of page text (the search proposal), and a keyboard shortcut that adds the current page. Neither design is approved yet, and both end with a list of open questions.
operations.details: The sync design prefers a shared folder to a server so that no account is needed. The search proposal estimates the index at about a tenth of the size of the pages it covers.

operations.summary: Contributor rules live in docs/CONTRIBUTING.md: every change comes with a test, a commit describes one change only, and a pull request needs one approving review before it is merged. Code style follows docs/STYLE.md, which asks for type hints on public functions, black formatting at 100 columns and no wildcard imports. Releases follow docs/RELEASING.md and are tagged by hand. CHANGELOG.md gets one line for each change a user can see.
operations.details: The FAQ and the architecture overview repeat some of these rules in shorter form; where they differ, CONTRIBUTING.md is the newer text. The Makefile that the release guide mentions is not part of this material.
